title: Demonstrate an understanding of the importance of marketing

lessons.title: Why marketing matters
lessons.html:
Growing is only half the job

A farmer can grow the best tomatoes in the district, but if nobody buys them, they rot and the money spent on seed, fertiliser and water is lost. Marketing means everything you do to get your product to a buyer and be paid a fair price. It is just as important as growing the crop or raising the animals.

What marketing includes

  • Finding out what buyers want.
  • Growing or raising what buyers want, when they want it.
  • Getting the product ready: picking, cleaning, sorting and packing.
  • Taking it to the buyer.
  • Agreeing on a price and getting paid.
  • Telling people about your product.

Who are the buyers?

BuyerWhat they often want
Neighbours and householdsFresh produce, fair price, small amounts
Spaza shops and hawkersRegular supply, good price so they can sell at a profit
Schools, clinics, restaurantsReliable delivery, clean produce, set amounts every week
SupermarketsLarge, steady amounts, high quality, proper packing
Fresh produce marketsGraded and packed produce in standard containers
Butchers and auctionsHealthy animals in good condition

Example

Lindiwe grows spinach. At first she sells only to neighbours, and much of her spinach goes to waste. She visits two spaza shops and a school kitchen nearby. They agree to buy bunches every week if she delivers on Mondays and Thursdays. Now she plants a new bed every two weeks so she always has spinach ready, and almost nothing goes to waste.

Remember: the best time to think about marketing is before you plant or buy animals. Then you grow what buyers really want.

lessons.title: Good marketing habits
lessons.html:
Know your buyer

Talk to buyers before you plant. Ask: What do you want to buy? How much? How often? What price? This helps you plant the right crop, the right amount, at the right time.

Quality matters

  • Harvest at the right time, not too early or too late.
  • Handle produce gently so it does not bruise.
  • Sort it: put good, even produce together. Remove damaged or rotten produce.
  • Keep produce clean and in the shade.
  • Pack in clean crates, bags or boxes.

Buyers come back to farmers who always bring good quality.

Be reliable

  • Deliver the amount you promised.
  • Deliver on the day and time you agreed.
  • If there is a problem, like hail damage, tell the buyer early.

Know your costs and the price

Write down what you spend to grow the crop. Then you know the lowest price you can accept. Check what other sellers charge. If your price is far higher, buyers may go elsewhere. If it is too low, you lose money.

Tell people about your product

  • A neat sign at your gate or stall.
  • Word of mouth: happy customers tell others.
  • WhatsApp or community groups to share what is ready this week.
  • A small sample for a new shop to try.

Timing

Prices often drop when everyone has the same crop at the same time, and rise when it is scarce. If you can have produce ready when others do not, you may get a better price.

Benefits of good marketing

  • Less waste.
  • Better and more regular income.
  • Loyal buyers who come back.
  • A good name for your farm.

Key points

  • Marketing means getting the product to a buyer at a fair price.
  • Talk to buyers before you plant.
  • Harvest, sort and pack carefully for good quality.
  • Be reliable with amounts and delivery times.
  • Know your costs, check prices and tell people about your product.
